free_tier.stated: 100 databases; 5 GB storage; 500 million rows read per month; 10 million rows written per month; 3 GB sync

per_object_cap.stated: 5 GB across all databases on Free; the plan table gives no per-database cap

retention.stated: a database is archived after 10 days of inactivity on a free plan, and an archived database must be unarchived before it can be used; a deleted database has no point-in-time restore on Free and the Free column shows 1-day audit logs
retention.notes: the archive clock is documented on the CLI and API reference pages, not on the pricing page

egress.terms: no egress charge and no transfer allowance is published; the metered quantities are rows read and rows written, so a byte of egress is not what is counted

interface_detail: libSQL over HTTP and WebSockets; the Turso CLI; a platform API
tooling: the turso CLI; libSQL client libraries; sqld for a local replica
chaining: a free SQLite replica per tenant suits multi-tenant read-heavy work that a single free Postgres cannot hold, provided something touches each database at least every 10 days, because the free plan archives an inactive one

limits.value: 500 million rows read and 10 million rows written per month
5 GB total across all databases; 100 databases
an inactive database is archived after 10 days on a free plan
no connection limit is published on the pricing page or the feature pages; recorded as a gap

identity_cost.detail: email signup; GitHub OAuth also offered

reliability_note: an inactive database on a free plan is archived after 10 days and must be unarchived before use; the archive is not a deletion and the data survives it
confidence_note: the pricing table was read today and its own meta description states 100 databases and 5 GB. The 10-day archive clock is from Turso's CLI reference, read the same day

evidence.proved: Free column: 100 databases, 5GB storage, 500 Million rows read, 10 Million rows written, 3GB sync, 1 day audit logs; Developer USD 4.99 gives unlimited databases and 9GB
'Databases get archived after 10 days of inactivity for users on a free plan'; the unarchive command restores one
the platform API exposes a group unarchive endpoint, so the archive state is reachable programmatically and not only through the CLI
an unauthenticated GET returns 401 with 'token contains an invalid number of segments', proving the platform API exists and is token-authenticated

notes: The 500-database and 9-GB figures in circulation are the Developer plan, not Free. The 5 GB is a total, so 100 databases average 50 MB each. The binding constraint is not either number: it is the 10-day archive, which a quarterly job meets first and which nothing on the pricing page states.
binding_note: 10 days of inactivity archives the database on the free plan, so a job that runs less often than that finds the database unavailable. The 5 GB total and the 10-million-row monthly write budget are larger than that clock allows a quarterly job to reach.
